title: The provider is guessed from the request shape, so a config key may only be called anthropic or openai
foundBy: user report (host): "Determining the target provider from the request shape (e.g. /messages -> anthropic) is very fragile. Can we instead adopt a URL convention like /c/<provider-name>/<cassette-name>"

evidence.verified: make check with an empty CS_VCR_HOME: prose, refs, oss and surface all report 0 errors, and every package passes. make test-smoke: TestReplayFixtures PASS, all 8 scenarios, 18.9s. That smoke run is the load-bearing one. It replays every committed cassette through the three real agents under the new prefix, with nothing re-recorded, which shows the extra segment is stripped before a request is keyed.

resolution: A base URL now carries /c/<provider>/<cassette>. The provider is a free key into `providers`, `default_provider` and `cassette_provider` are gone, and `classify` is gone with them. The surface is still read from the path, and replay still reads no provider configuration.
details:
`classify` maps a surface to a hardcoded provider name. `/messages` becomes `anthropic`, and `/responses` and `/chat/completions` become `openai`. A provider entry is reachable by path only if it is called one of those two names. Every other name needs a workaround, and this repository's own scenario matrix carries both of them.

`opencode-fireworks` pins its cassette. `test/agents/scenario.go` says why: "Fireworks is not a provider cs-vcr routes to by path, every OpenAI-shaped request looks the same". `claude-code-fireworks` avoids the pin by naming a Fireworks endpoint `anthropic`, so its config key states a vendor its `base_url` contradicts.

The two workarounds rest on a third mechanism. `default_provider` absorbs whatever neither the path nor the Anthropic-specific headers identified. Absorbing is what rule R1a refuses for the cassette, on the grounds that "a default to absorb it into would make a mistyped base URL look like it worked". A request that lands on the wrong provider is forwarded there with the client's credential attached, and recorded as though it were the answer.

The request already carries one name the operator chose, which is the cassette prefix. Carrying the provider beside it as `/c/<provider>/<cassette>` states what the client is pointed at. That retires `default_provider`, `cassette_provider` and `classify` together. The surface is unaffected. It is read from the path because that is what keys the body, and replay reads it while reading no provider configuration at all.

notes.text: Two follow-ups this left alone. The claude-code-fireworks scenario can now name its provider entry `fireworks` instead of `anthropic`, which needs a re-record because the entry name is recorded as cassette metadata. And a config file carrying default_provider or cassette_provider now fails at startup under rule R43, which is the migration this change asks of anyone upgrading.

Followed up in review. The claude-code-fireworks scenario now names its provider entry `fireworks`, so the entry no longer states a vendor its base_url contradicts. The cassettes still carry `anthropic` as recorded metadata until they are recorded again. The printer's provider is an argument rather than a per-client default, and the prefix is one word in the code as well: Prefix, RoutePrefix, ErrNoPrefix, and the no_prefix and bad_prefix replies.

The shipped provider set grew to four: anthropic, openai, chatgpt and fireworks, each at its own endpoint. Naming the provider in the base URL is what allows the third, because openai and chatgpt are one vendor at two endpoints and a request cannot be told which it meant. A deployment reaching any of the four now writes no configuration file, and `cs-vcr config codex` prints the block each endpoint actually needs: a version segment and a key for one, neither for the other.

The cassettes were recorded again, so the metadata matches the entries that serve them: claude-code-fireworks records `fireworks` and codex-chatgpt records `chatgpt`, including the GET /models probe that opens a Codex session. Every step is a 200, and `make ci` replays all eight.
